caption:
The sack coat is half a century older than the Brooks Brothers suit that made it famous.

The Museum at FIT dates the American sack suit to the 1840s and 1850s, when it was leisure wear with no place in formal town dress. Its back is cut in two panels where a frock coat had four. Brooks Brothers sold a plain version as the No. 1 Sack Suit, dated to 1895 or 1901 depending on the account. The Ivy League look later made the loose, dartless cut its own.

Connected to the lounge suit, frock coat, J. Press, the three-roll-two front and the hooked vent.
